CROSS-ALBUM SLOT DECLARATIONS -- the allowlist tools/check_album_provenance.py gates.

An album slot normally holds a file encoded from that album's OWN source folder. A
slot that holds a file from a different album's folder is a decision about a
RECORDING -- the same performance shipped twice under different release names -- and
it must be written down here, with its evidence, or the gate fails.

WHY A SEPARATE FILE. build_map.py rewrites soundtracks/track_map.json from scratch, so a
declaration stored there can be erased by a regeneration. albums_manifest.json is
NOT regenerated by anything -- it is hand-authored and gen_albums.py only READS it
and writes the generated albums.json from it -- but it is still the map that a
regeneration of the pool re-derives against, and a declaration parked in a
regenerated file is not safe. A declaration that a build step can silently delete
is not a declaration, so this file is owned by no generator.

WHY A DECLARATION AND NOT A HASH. track_map.json already pins every .dsp sha256 to
the source FLAC it was encoded from, and the encoder is byte-deterministic on a
pinned toolchain, so the BYTES are already proven. What nothing proved was whether
the file in a given slot is the recording that album is supposed to have: pointing
a slot at any other valid track passed every existing check.

THE RULE, exactly: for each album, the gate derives that album's own source folder
from track_map.json by name (see check_album_provenance.py's docstring), and every
slot whose file traces elsewhere must appear here with the matching album, slot and
file. The set must be EXACTLY the live bindings -- a stale, wrong, non-cross-album
or duplicated declaration fails too, so this list cannot rot. `slot` is the index
into that album's albums_manifest.json listing and is part of the identity: album
order is gameplay (music_core.cpp applyAlbumLevel maps a level to that index), so a
moved slot is a different decision and must be re-declared deliberately.

To see the live set after a deliberate change: python3 tools/check_album_provenance.py
prints the derived album->folder table and names every undeclared slot.

aliases.reason: retired re-rip, user decision 2026-10-12: this slot previously held this album's own gamerip file at listing slot 1 (source tempest3000_soundtrack/02.flac, 133 s), which is NOT a Tempest 3000 composition but a re-rip of this same Tempest 2000 recording -- measured on this machine 2026-10-11, that source matches 'Thermal Resolution' from +2.16 s at ncc 0.87-0.99 (median 0.97) at a constant lag, i.e. the DVD-Video rip split the one Tempest 2000 track across two of its audio tracks. The retired slot-1 file was 41_tem_02.dsp, displayed as 'Thermal Resolution (T3 edit)', and the dropped sibling at slot 2 was 42_tem_03.dsp, displayed as 'Thermal Resolution (T3 edit 2)'; both retired pool stems are named here deliberately, alongside their source paths and ncc evidence, so a reader holding an old save, an old rip listing, or an old track_map.json that still lists them has something to grep for. The pool file aliased here traces to tempest2000_soundtrack, not tempest3000_soundtrack, so it is cross-album for this listing. Slot INDEX preserved, so slot 1 still plays this recording; note that applyAlbumLevel divides the 100 levels by the album's usable-track count, so dropping slot 2 moved every band boundary in this album -- slot 1's own included, levels 6-11 -> 7-12; the sibling re-rip that held slot 2 (source tempest3000_soundtrack/03.flac, 103 s, ncc 0.84-1.00 from +135.85 s) was dropped entirely rather than aliased to this same file, because gen_albums.py refuses a duplicate within one album, so the listing went 19 -> 18 slots.

Offset-invariant probe matching (validated 0.9996 for a degraded same recording vs 0.124 for a different track) scores the pair at r >= 0.99, so the Tempest 2000 encode is aliased here instead of shipping a second copy of the same recording. Slot index preserved so this album's level bands are unchanged.

recording: it is the TxK recording; the retired Space Giraffe copy was the same performance looped (lag-searched cross-correlation ncc 0.9495 at lag ~0 and 0.9494 at lag ~293.28 s, self-ncc 0.9955 with a seam click at 293.257 s); the long version's extra 10.06 s closing reprise is knowingly dropped; source FLAC retained at soundtracks/Space_Giraffe/01.flac so the decision is reversible; slot index preserved to keep the level bands identical.
